author: A Robot
objectives: Identify and name the four chambers, four heart valves, and major vessels of the heart.
Trace the path of blood through the heart's dual circulation.
Explain the structural differences between the left and right ventricles.
Describe the role of valves in preventing backflow in the cardiac cycle.

modules.description: An exploration of the external and internal structure of the human heart, identifying the chambers, valves, and primary vessels.
modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Identify the four chambers of the heart.
Locate the major vessels entering and leaving the heart.
instructions: Inspect the 3D heart model from all angles.
Observe the labels identifying the chambers and valves.

clips.changeMeaning: Introduce the heart structure and show basic anatomy.
clips.narration: Welcome to your study of the human heart. Observe the four chambers: the right and left atria, and the right and left ventricles.

clips.changeMeaning: Highlight valves and major vessels for identification.
clips.narration: Key structures include the tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral, and aortic valves, as well as major vessels like the aorta and vena cava. These act as the traffic controllers for blood flow.

modules.description: A demonstration of the blood's journey through the dual-loop circulation, emphasizing the differences between the pulmonary and systemic circuits.
modules.author: A Robot
educationalObjectives: Trace the path of blood through the heart.
Distinguish between the pulmonary and systemic circuits.
Relate ventricular wall thickness to pressure requirements.
instructions: Observe the color-coded flow of blood.
Compare the thickness of the left and right ventricular walls.

components.text: Blood Flow Path: Blue (Deoxy) to Red (Oxy)

clips.changeMeaning: Highlight the right side of the heart (pulmonary circuit).
clips.narration: Blood enters the right side, deoxygenated. It travels through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle, then through the pulmonary valve to the lungs. Notice the thinner myocardium compared to the left.

clips.changeMeaning: Highlight the left side of the heart (systemic circuit).
clips.narration: Oxygenated blood returns to the left atrium, passes the mitral valve into the left ventricle. This chamber is thick-walled, as it must pump blood through the entire body.

clips.changeMeaning: Final view of the heart cycle.
clips.narration: Together, these circuits ensure oxygen delivery to all tissues and gas exchange in the lungs. Remember, these valves ensure one-way traffic, preventing backflow during the cardiac cycle.
